name: Clurichaun
description: The clurichaun is a solitary fairy of Irish folklore: a small, red-faced, perpetually drunk male sprite who haunts wine cellars, breweries, and pubs, protecting the household's drink if respected and souring it if mistreated.

aliases.name: Cluricaune
aliases.meaning: Variant spelling used by T. Crofton Croker

aliases.name: Naggeneen
aliases.meaning: Pet-name from naigín, 'noggin' (a small drinking measure)

origin: Reports cluster in the southern half of Ireland — particularly Munster (Cork, Tipperary, Limerick, Waterford) — but regional variants are recorded across Leinster, parts of Ulster, and west into Connacht.
